import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 849

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/849](https://www.erdosproblems.com/849)
-/

open Nat

namespace Erdos849

/--
Is it true that, for every integer $t\geq1$, there is some integer $a$ such that ${n \choose k} = a$
with $1\leq k \le \frac{n}{2}$ has exactly $t$ solutions?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_849 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ t ≥ 1, ∃ a : ℕ,
      {n : ℕ | ∃ k ≥ 1, 2 * k ≤ n ∧ choose n k = a}.ncard = t := by
  sorry

end Erdos849

reformulations.difference: Lean counts distinct values of n admitting an admissible k, rather than explicitly counting solution pairs (n, k). It also takes a in ℕ instead of allowing an arbitrary integer.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For fixed n, k ↦ Nat.choose n k is strictly increasing on 0 ≤ k ≤ floor(n/2). Consequently, projection (n,k) ↦ n is a bijection between the admissible solution pairs and the set counted by Lean. Furthermore, every admissible solution satisfies 2 ≤ n ≤ choose n k = a, so the solution sets are finite and no integer a < 2 can realize a positive count. Thus restricting a to ℕ loses no witnesses, and Set.ncard cannot introduce an infinite-set default-value discrepancy. The corresponding quantified equivalence, including integer a and explicit finiteness of the pair set, was proved as Review849.integer_source_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorryAx.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/849 (read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/849; includes the exact formulas, remarks, and bibliography)
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/ and https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html (paper collection indexes; the 1996 paper text was not located)
review.notes: Checked the sole declaration against the source's exact LaTeX statement and remarks. The source still records the problem as OPEN; its report that Erdős and Singmaster expected a negative answer does not resolve the question or conflict with answer(sorry). Quantifier scope, exact cardinality, and both bounds on k agree. Lean experiments proved finiteness, emptiness for a = 0 and 1, and the singleton case a = 2; computations reproduced the source's three solutions for a = 120 and four for a = 3003. The scratch file compiles successfully, and the equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependency. No repository files were edited.
